chunks: From him, from al-Baraqi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynab, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), asking him about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the month of Ramadan from the beginning of the night, and delayed the ghusl (ritual bath) until the dawn broke. He wrote back to me in his own handwriting, and I recognized it, while he was in the midst of performing ghusl from his janabah, completing his fast, and there was nothing upon him.

key_terms.أَجۡنَبَ: Became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one delays ghusl until after Fajr in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that delaying ghusl until after Fajr does not invalidate the Ramadan fast, a ruling confirmed by Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) through a personal note attached to a companion's letter. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the state of major impurity (junub) at the time of dawn does not preclude the validity of the fast, distinguishing it from the requirement of fasting intention (niyyah). This ruling underscores the practical ease in Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity obligations relative to the daily fast.
